$comment: Advisories this build knowingly ships with, each with a reason and an expiry.
An advisory not listed here fails the gate. An entry past its expiry fails the
gate. An entry that no longer matches anything also fails the gate, so the list
cannot quietly rot into a permanent allowance.

why: Denial of service through infinite loops in the ICNS, JXL and HEIF parsers.
There is no version to move to: the advisories cover <=2.0.2 and 2.0.2 is the
latest published release. npm's own suggested fix is a major downgrade of Expo
to 53, which would take React Native back three years and is not a fix.
It reaches this project only through metro, which reads image dimensions while
bundling. It is never installed into an application binary and never sees a
file a user opens — the images it parses are the ones already committed to this
repository, so triggering it requires control of the source tree, at which
point the loop is the least of the problems.
Revisit when image-size publishes a fix and metro adopts it. The expiry is
there so this is re-argued rather than inherited.
Cubic-time decoding of malformed percent-encoded input (CVE-2026-45822): 0.2.2
spends 32 s on 400 malformed escapes. The fix is 0.5.0, and it cannot be installed
here. 0.3.0 onwards is ESM-only, and the only dependent is query-string 7.1.3, which
`require`s this package and calls the result; every expo-router 57 release pins
query-string ^7.1.3, and npm's own suggested fix is expo-router 5.1.11, four SDKs
back. An override to 0.5.0 would hand query-string a module namespace, not a function.
Path: apps/mobile -> expo-router -> query-string 7.1.3 -> decode-uri-component 0.2.2,
bundled into the mobile app. expo-router parses incoming links with its own
URLSearchParams-based fork, so the only caller that decodes is the vendored React
Navigation getStateFromPath it replaces; that is an argument about today's call graph,
not a control. The control is the fix itself: patches/decode-uri-component+0.2.2.patch
backports 0.5.0's single-pass decoder (upstream fa479da) and keeps 0.2.2's
`+`-to-space conversion, so nothing else about the 0.2 contract moves.
verify-dependency-patches checks the installed file's digest and decodes the
pathological input. npm audit matches on the version number, which a patch cannot
change, so the advisory still needs this entry.
Owner: Iroha PDF maintainers.
Revisit when expo-router takes query-string 9.5 or later (which accepts
decode-uri-component 0.5) or stops depending on it. Remove the patch and this entry
together.
